skill.name: plan-harder
skill.description: Creates detailed, phased implementation plans for software bugs, features, and technical tasks after researching the codebase and clarifying requirements.
skill.summary: Turn a software request into a reviewed, testable, sprint-based implementation plan.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and a fenced template. The skill contains no shell execution or prompt injection evidence.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 71 uses Markdown inline code formatting for the literal filename suffix `-plan.md`. It does not invoke Ruby, a shell, or any command.

Line 75 formats another example output filename as inline Markdown code. No shell or Ruby execution is requested.
Lines 92 through 137 are a fenced Markdown plan template. The backticks delimit documentation and do not execute its contents.

content.value_statement: Complex engineering requests often lack clear sequencing, validation, and risk controls. This skill converts them into researched, phased plans with atomic tasks and review.
actual_capabilities: Investigates repository architecture, dependencies, related components, and established implementation patterns before planning.
Uses targeted questions to clarify scope, constraints, priorities, edge cases, and success criteria.
Organizes work into phased sprints that each produce a runnable, testable increment.
Breaks sprints into atomic tasks with locations, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation steps.
Reviews plans for missing steps, risks, ambiguities, rollback needs, and lifecycle concerns.
Generates a kebab-case plan filename and saves the completed plan as Markdown.
limitations: Creates plans only and does not implement changes.
Requires repository context for accurate file paths and architecture details.
Estimates complexity qualitatively and does not calculate delivery dates or staffing needs.
May require user answers when requirements, constraints, or priorities are unclear.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature
use_cases.description: Research an existing application and produce phased implementation work with acceptance criteria, tests, deployment checks, and rollback steps.

use_cases.title: Structure a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Trace a defect across related components and define small, verifiable tasks that address root cause and regression coverage.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Technical Initiative
use_cases.description: Separate a complex change into demoable sprints with dependencies, parallel work, release gates, and identified risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for this bug: [describe bug]. Research the repository, clarify unknowns, and save a phased plan with tests and rollback steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused defect

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for [feature] in [repository]. Include architecture research, dependencies, atomic tasks, acceptance criteria, and a validation checklist for each sprint.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a new capability

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for migrating [current system] to [target system]. Compare existing patterns and include compatibility, sequencing, rollout, observability, and rollback work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cross-Team Initiative
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for [complex initiative]. Map workstreams, dependencies, security and performance risks, release gates, test strategy, deployment stages, and rollback decisions.

output_examples.input: Plan harder for adding Google sign-in to our web application.
output_examples.output: A Markdown plan covering authentication research, configuration, callback handling, interface changes, tests, rollout checks, risks, and rollback steps across demoable sprints.

output_examples.input: Plan harder for fixing duplicate invoice creation during payment retries.
output_examples.output: A phased plan tracing retry behavior, defining idempotency changes, adding concurrency tests, validating observability, and preparing a reversible deployment.

best_practices: Provide the repository, desired outcome, constraints, and known acceptance criteria before requesting a plan.
Answer clarification questions with explicit priorities and firm scope boundaries.
Review every sprint for a demonstrable outcome, practical validation, and a reversible deployment path.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill when immediate implementation is required.
Do not accept placeholder tasks that omit concrete files, dependencies, acceptance criteria, or tests.
Do not treat complexity estimates as delivery commitments.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a saved Markdown implementation plan organized into phased sprints, atomic tasks, validation steps, risks, and rollback guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill implement the plan?
faq.answer: No. It researches, clarifies, writes, reviews, and updates the plan without changing the product code.

faq.question: How does it handle unclear requirements?
faq.answer: It asks targeted questions about scope, constraints, priorities, edge cases, and success criteria before finalizing the plan.

faq.question: Where is the plan saved?
faq.answer: It creates a kebab-case filename based on the request and adds the suffix -plan.md.

faq.question: Can it plan large initiatives?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize complex work into sequential sprints, explicit dependencies, parallel tasks, release gates, and verification steps.

faq.question: Does the plan include risk review?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for missing steps, ambiguous decisions, edge cases, lifecycle concerns, deployment risks, and rollback needs.
